title: Ada and the Letter
premise: Retired detective Coral Nystrom, now barely keeping her bookshop afloat, receives an anonymous letter hinting that the three 'accidents' she quietly solved were rehearsals for something larger. When a stranger is found dead wearing clothes lifted from her own closet, staged with details only the original case files could contain, Coral realizes the killer is someone who studied her methods — perhaps a former colleague, perhaps the one suspect who walked free years ago. Racing a killer who anticipates her every move, Coral plants false clues in her own shop, luring him into confessing on tape, but the trap nearly costs her life before the truth surfaces: the killer is the quiet archivist who preserved those very case files, avenging a sister the law failed. In the end Coral must choose between handing him to justice and letting a broken man vanish, choosing instead to expose the old cover-up that made him.
about_author: Noor Amberdale is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent two decades watching cases slip through procedural cracks. She writes mysteries about ordinary people forced to become instruments of justice when institutions fail them.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Returns Bin
chapters.summary: Coral Nystrom finds a typed letter slipped inside a returned paperback, referencing details from three deaths she privately solved — details never made public. That night, police knock: a body in the harbor dressed in her own missing clothes. Told from Coral's POV, the chapter establishes her loneliness, failing bookshop, and dread that her hidden past has found her. Emotional beat: unease curdling into personal violation.

chapters.title: Details Only the Dead Would Know
chapters.summary: Coral examines the crime scene and recognizes her own investigative signatures replicated in the staging — a deliberate message. She pulls her old notes and discovers all four victims connect to a 1998 drowning ruled accidental. Alternating briefly with Detective Ilsa Voss's skeptical POV, tension builds as Coral realizes she's both suspect and target. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by fear of being framed.

chapters.title: A Trap Built of Paper
chapters.summary: Coral stages fake evidence in her bookshop and feeds a false timeline through Voss, betting the killer watches her the way she once watched suspects. The stakeout works too well: she confronts the archivist, Elias Brandt, who reveals his sister was the 1998 victim and the file was buried by a now-powerful official. His confession is recorded — then he takes Coral hostage. Emotional beat: triumph flipping to terror at gunpoint.

chapters.title: What the Law Couldn't Read
chapters.summary: Coral talks Elias down using the same patience she used on grieving families, convincing him to surrender the proof of the cover-up rather than die for it. Voss arrests the implicated official; Elias faces trial, and Coral testifies to what the law ignored. Closing in her POV, she reopens the bookshop with a new shelf: unsolved cases, waiting. Emotional beat: weary catharsis and guarded hope.
